newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply down on Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply down on Wall Street fall.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished sharply lower on Saturday as profit-taking intensified following Wall Street's overnight plunge, brokers said.
The weighted index ended down 105.19 points, or 1.22 percent, at 8,487.89. Turnover was a hectic T$149 billion in the abbreivated Saturday session.

Electronic shares led Saturday's fall, down 2.87 percent, on worries over a probe of certain types of memory chips imported from Korea and Taiwan following a finding by the U.S. International Trade Commission, brokers said.

The U.S. International Trade Commission said it found there was a reasonable indication that U.S. industry was hurt by the imports of static random access memory semiconductors at what U.S. manufacturer Micron Technology Inc had alleged was less than fair value.
"Several Taiwan SRAM makers plunged over the news," said Oliver Fang, an analyst of National Securities.
United Microelectronics Corp fell by the daily seven percent limit, losing T$5 to T$67.5. Winbond was down T$2.1 or 4.44 percent to T$45.2.
"The market has risen a lot recently and it is especially sensitive about such bearish news at the moment," Fang said.
"Technically, it opted for a correction as well," he added.

Brokers said investors also largely discounted imminent direct crossings between Taiwan and China after Taiwan approved on Friday four shippers from arch rival China to sail directly across the Taiwan strait, ending a ban dating to 1949.
"The market has expected this to happen. It's not a surprise," Fang said.
But brokers said shipping shares may have a chance to rise once the direct crossings actually take place.
The central bank's recent squeeze in banking system liquidity would force the stock market to consolidate next week, brokers said.
"The central bank makes very clear that it wants to cool the stock fever and the market is aware of the signal," Fang said.

Deputy central banker Hsu Chia-tung warned on Wednesday that Taiwan's stock market turnover rate and price-earnings ratio were far higher than other countries' and urged investors to be "risk-conscious and extra careful".
A range of 8,200-8,700 range was seen for next week.
